The most material change is the divergence between improving proxy breadth and weak cross-horizon price and flow data. BTC and ETH posted negative 12-hour and 72-hour returns with negative aggressive quote flow, while ETH experienced a marked CFGI deterioration and weaker latest order-book conditions. Against this, breadth improved to 80%, BTC latest microstructure became positive, and ETHBTC remained above 0.03 for 168 hourly closes. The combined evidence is therefore more consistent with a paused or failed transition and possible short-horizon pullback risk than with either confirmed broad continuation or established late-cycle deterioration. Forecast candidates are unratified research objects only. Confidence is reduced by the unavailable and contract-violating one-hour horizon, mixed observation ages, lower-bound liquidation aggregates, non-canonical breadth proxies, and absent macro data.
